steps.title: Import Vue and defineErrorCaptured hook
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the defineErrorCaptured hook from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both Vue and defineErrorCaptured from 'vue'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing from a package
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue package and defineErrorCaptured hook are imported, making them available for use in the component.
successCriteria: Vue and defineErrorCaptured are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue and defineErrorCaptured, which are essential for creating error boundaries in Vue.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both Vue and defineErrorCaptured from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import both Vue and defineErrorCaptured from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create main ErrorBoundary component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named ErrorBoundary that returns a template with a single <div> element.
steps.hint: Define a component using the defineComponent function from Vue, or use a simple function that returns a template.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and defineErrorCaptured from 'vue'

// Create your ErrorBoundary component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional ErrorBoundary component is created with a basic template structure.
successCriteria: ErrorBoundary component is defined and returns a template with a <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the ErrorBoundary component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the component, but make sure it returns a template with a <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't properly defined yet. Create a Vue component named ErrorBoundary that returns a template.

steps.title: Initialize error state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside your ErrorBoundary component, initialize a reactive state variable called 'error' using Vue's ref function, setting its initial value to null.
steps.hint: Use the ref function from Vue to create a reactive reference. Remember to call ref() with null as the argument.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a reactive state variable
const count = ref(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a reactive 'error' variable that starts as null and can track error information.
successCriteria: A ref called 'error' is declared inside setup() with null as its initial value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the error state. This reactive variable will allow your component to track and respond to errors.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using Vue's ref function to create a reactive variable called 'error' with null as the initial value inside the setup() function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a reactive state variable called 'error' using Vue's ref function, initialized to null, inside the component's setup() function.

steps.title: Initialize error info state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, initialize a reactive ref called 'errorInfo' with null as its initial value.
steps.hint: Use the ref function you imported earlier to create another reactive reference. Place this after your existing error state initialization.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: initializing another reactive state
const userInfo = ref(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a second reactive state variable 'errorInfo' initialized to null, ready to store error information.
successCriteria: The setup function contains a 'errorInfo' ref initialized with null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the errorInfo reactive state. This will allow your component to track detailed error information.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're creating a ref called 'errorInfo' and initializing it with null inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires initializing a reactive ref called 'errorInfo' with null as its initial value inside the setup function.

steps.title: Implement defineErrorCaptured hook
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, implement the defineErrorCaptured hook to capture errors and update the error state.
steps.hint: Use defineErrorCaptured to create a hook that receives error and info parameters, then sets the error ref to the captured error.
steps.expectedOutcome: The defineErrorCaptured hook is implemented to capture errors and update the error state.
successCriteria: defineErrorCaptured hook is implemented with a function that receives error and info parameters and sets the error ref.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the defineErrorCaptured hook to capture errors.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your defineErrorCaptured hook properly receives error and info parameters and updates the error ref.
steps.feedbackWrong: The defineErrorCaptured hook isn't implemented correctly. It should capture errors and update the error state.

steps.title: Add template structure with conditional rendering
steps.instruction: Add a template section to your ErrorBoundary component that conditionally shows an error message when an error exists, otherwise shows the slot content.
steps.hint: In Vue, components can have a template property. Use v-if to check if error.value exists, and v-else for the default slot.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ErrorBoundary component will have a template that conditionally renders error content or slot content based on whether an error exists.
successCriteria: The component has a template property with v-if checking error.value and v-else showing a <slot />.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the template structure with conditional rendering. This will display error messages when they occur, otherwise show the normal content.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your template includes both the error display condition (v-if) and the slot content (v-else).
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure isn't quite right. Remember to add a template property with v-if to check error.value and v-else to show the slot content.

steps.title: Display error message in template
steps.instruction: Inside the template section of your ErrorBoundary component, add a paragraph element that displays the error message from the error state when an error exists.
steps.hint: Use the error ref value in a conditional block to show the error message. You can access it with error.value.
steps.analogousExample: // Similar: displaying state in template
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the captured error message when an error occurs.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added inside the template that displays error.value when error exists.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the error message display to your ErrorBoundary component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're displaying the actual error message from the error state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error message isn't being displayed correctly. Check that you're accessing error.value and using proper template syntax.

steps.title: Display error info in template
steps.instruction: In the template's error display section, add a <pre> element that shows the errorInfo.value.componentStack value when an error exists.
steps.hint: Use v-if to conditionally render the <pre> element only when error exists. Inside the <pre>, display errorInfo.value.componentStack.
steps.analogousExample: // Similar: conditional display of error details
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show error details including the component stack trace when an error occurs.
successCriteria: A <pre> element is added inside the template that conditionally displays errorInfo.value.componentStack when error exists.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added error information display to your ErrorBoundary component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're displaying errorInfo.value.componentStack inside a <pre> element that only shows when error exists.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error information isn't displayed correctly. Add a <pre> element with v-if="error" that shows errorInfo.value.componentStack.

steps.title: Create child component that throws error
steps.instruction: Create a new component named ErrorTrigger that contains a button which throws an error when clicked.
steps.hint: Define a new component with a setup function that returns an object containing a method to throw an error, and a template with a button that calls that method.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new ErrorTrigger component is created with a button that will throw an error when clicked.
successCriteria: The ErrorTrigger component is defined with a setup method that returns a throwError function, and a template containing a button with @click="throwError".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the ErrorTrigger component that will throw an error when its button is clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it has a button that triggers an error when clicked.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ErrorTrigger component is missing or doesn't have the correct structure. It should have a setup method with a throwError function and a button in the template that calls it.

steps.title: Wrap child component with ErrorBoundary
steps.instruction: In the main app, wrap the ErrorTrigger component with the ErrorBoundary component to catch its errors.
steps.hint: Place the ErrorTrigger component inside the ErrorBoundary component's slot.
steps.analogousExample:
// Wrapping a component with another component
<ErrorBoundary>
  <ErrorTrigger />
</ErrorBoundary>
steps.expectedOutcome: The ErrorBoundary component now wraps the ErrorTrigger component, allowing it to catch errors thrown by the child.
successCriteria: ErrorTrigger is placed inside ErrorBoundary component tags.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wrapped the ErrorTrigger component with ErrorBoundary. Now when the button is clicked, the error will be caught and displayed by the ErrorBoundary.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure ErrorTrigger is placed directly inside the ErrorBoundary component tags.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ErrorTrigger component needs to be wrapped by the ErrorBoundary component. Place ErrorTrigger between opening and closing ErrorBoundary tags.
